VIII.}}</noinclude>God vvere your father: verely you vvould loue me. for from God I proceded, and came: for I came not of my self, but he sent me: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=43}}† VVhy doe you not knovv my speach? Because you can not heare my vvord. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=44}}† You are of your father the Diuel, and the desires of your father you vvil doe. he vvas a {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. Augustine compareth Heretikes in their spiritual murder by driuing Christian men out of the Church, to the Diuel that droue our parents out of Paradise. ''Cont. lit. Petil. li. 2, c. 13''.}}∷ mankiller from the beginning, and he stoode not in the veritie: because veritie is not in him. vvhen he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his owne, because he is a lyer, and the father thereof. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=45}}† But because I say the veritie, you beleeue me not. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=46}}† VVhich of you shal argue me of sinne? If I say the veritie: vvhy doe you not beleeue me? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=47}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō PASSION Sunday.}}He that is of God, heareth the vvordes of God. Therfore you heare not, because you are not of God. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=48}}† The Iewes therfore ansvvered, and said to him, Doe not we say vvel that thou art a Samaritane, and hast a diuil? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=49}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ He denieth not that he is a Samaritane, because he is our keeper or protector, as the vvord signifieth, and because he is in deede that merciful Samaritane in the parable of the wounded man Luc. 10, 33. ''Aug. tract. 43 in Ioan''.}}∷ I haue no deuil: but I doe honour my Father, and you haue dishonoured me. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=50}}† but I seeke not mine ovvne glorie. there is that seeketh and iudgeth.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=51}}† Amen, amen I say to you, If any man keepe my vvord, he shal not see death for euer. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=52}}† The Ievves therfore said, Now vve haue knovven that thou hast a deuil. Abraham is dead, and the Prophets: and thou saiest, If any man keepe my vvord, he shal not tast death for euer. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=53}}† VVhy, art thou greater then our father Abraham, vvho is dead? and the Prophets are dead. VVhom doest thou make thy self? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=54}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} answered, If I doe glorifie my self, my glorie is nothing. it is my father that glorifieth me, vvhom you say that he is your God. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=55}}† And you haue not knovven him, but I knovv him. And if I shal say that I knovv him not: I shal be like to you, a lyer. But I doe knovv him, and doe keepe his vvord. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=56}}† Abraham your father reioyced that he might see my day: and he savv, and vvas glad. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=57}}† The Ievves therfore said to him, Thou hast not yet fiftie yeres, and hast thou seen Abraham? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=58}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, Amen, amen I say to you, before that Abraham vvas made, I am. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=59}}† They tooke stones therfore to cast at him. but {{sc|Iesvs}} hid him self, and vvent out of the temple.⊣

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. VIII.}}}}

''34. Amen, amen.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Why ''Amen, amen'', is not translated.}}''What is it (saith S. Augustine vpon this place) when our Lord saith'', Amen, amen? ''He doth much commend and vrge the thing that he so vttereth, doubling it. It is a certaine othe of his, if a man may so say. for Amen in Hebrue signifieth'' verum, a truth. ''Yet is it not translated, whereas it might haue been said'', verum, verum ''dico vobis. but neither the'' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=*See the preface, & Annot. in ''Apocal. c. 19. 4''.}}''Greeke interpreter durst doe it, nor the Latin. the Hebrue word hath remained stil, that so it might be the more esteemed. Tract. 41 in Ioan. By vvhich vvordes and the like'' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=* ''Ἀμὴν, ἀμὴν''.}}''recorded in other places of this nevv Testament, the Reader may see great reason, why vve also say'', Amen, amen, ''and durst not translate it and such like wordes into our English tongue''.<noinclude>{{rh|||CHAP.}}</noinclude>
